summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: an ordinary maintenance problem is already open on the wall. Middle image: Astra asks for scale while Zib stays practical. Closing image: the absurd replacement delay becomes the actual pressure.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Maintenance bay establishing view: the coolant-balancing unit is open in the wall under a red temporary-flow warning while Zib studies the cracked stabilizer bracket.
PANEL 2 — Astra arrives with coffee and unrelated paperwork, asking whether this is ordinary-annoying while Zib keeps one hand inside the unit.
PANEL 3 — Zib identifies the bracket and gestures toward the procurement display rather than dramatizing the failure.
PANEL 4 — The nineteen-day replacement ETA fills the display beside Zib's deadpan counterpoint.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Of course it's the bracket. I said it would be the bracket in spring.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: You also said the hot-water dispenser would last another decade.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: I was right about the dispenser until Jax made soup in it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: What is the actual replacement time?

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Nineteen days. The machine can barely manage nineteen minutes like this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: That's a very specific kind of inconvenience.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay, continuing directly from the delayed-part discovery. Opening image: Astra confirms the delay is real. Middle image: Jax is folded into the repair without ceremony. Closing image: corporate process arrives as paperwork around a small mechanical problem.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra reads the nineteen-day ETA twice while Zib continues working without looking up.
PANEL 2 — Astra rejects procurement fraud as Jax arrives with the handheld reader and realizes he has been absorbed into the morning repair.
PANEL 3 — Astra assigns Jax the readings directly at the unit.
PANEL 4 — Pixa opens the temporary-material authorization form beside them; its overbuilt title lands against the simple physical job.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: If we wait nineteen days, we spend three weeks working around this wall.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Yes. That's why I'm trying to make a safe temporary repair.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I brought the reader. And don't tell Glorp; I washed it first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: There is an approved temporary deviation path.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: How many people have to agree to it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: More than it takes to fix the bracket.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: Mira is doing ordinary retained-sample work beside the repair. Middle image: two samples behave differently under simple physical tests. Closing image: curiosity appears before interpretation.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — At the nearby lab bench, Mira works through sealed residue samples retained from earlier incidents.
PANEL 2 — One brittle fragment crumbles under the probe while a denser fragment clicks against the steel test block.
PANEL 3 — Mira stops mid-test; Zib notices from the open wall unit and asks which kind of 'huh' this is.
PANEL 4 — Mira keeps the denser fragment raised, interested but unwilling to name it useful or dangerous yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: I kept the samples from the break-room vent. I thought one might be useful eventually.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Please tell me you're not going to patch a coolant unit with soup dust.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: I'm comparing physical behavior. The sample from the cable seam is different.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Different how?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: It doesn't crush in quite the same way. It might be nothing, but I want to know.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Lab Work Area, continuing the test. Opening image: Mira checks that the difference repeats. Middle image: the scientific result becomes understandable without becoming grand. Closing image: uncertainty is preserved as a useful boundary.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira repeats the same compression test on both samples and records the divergence.
PANEL 2 — Zib asks for plain language; Mira holds the two fragments side by side and gives it to him.
PANEL 3 — Astra accepts the simple observable distinction, but Mira raises a hand before anyone turns it into an explanation.
PANEL 4 — Mira states that she still does not know why; Astra is visibly relieved by the limit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: I ran it again. Same result. If I'm wrong, at least I'm wrong consistently.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: That is not as reassuring to me as it is to you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Are we talking about a repair or a discovery?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Right now? A measurement. Which is already more interesting than my morning.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Keep it a measurement until we can prove something else.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: Glorp reviews the temporary repair authorization with visible alarm. Middle image: Zib speaks from inside the wall compartment. Closing image: Jax raises the flow reader. Astra nods once. No ceremony.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp reviews the temporary repair authorization with visible alarm.
PANEL 2 — Glorp taps the word TEMPORARY.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb reads beside them.
PANEL 4 — Zib speaks from inside the wall compartment.
PANEL 5 — Glorp deletes lines from the form until only three labeled fields remain.
PANEL 6 — Jax raises the flow reader. Astra nods once. No ceremony.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: This authorization describes a temporary repair, not an experiment.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Fine. I'll do the repair with a regular clamp. The sample is filling a gap, not holding the station together.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: Could we at least agree who stays to watch it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I can watch the meter. I'm not going to wash its dishes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't suggesting dishes. I was asking when the inspection ends.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: If it holds, we'll tell you. If it doesn't, you'll hear us.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Lab Work Area. Opening image: the strange material is tested safely off-line. Middle image: it survives some conditions and fails another. Closing image: the test produces a useful limitation rather than a discovery claim.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira and Zib build a small off-line test rig away from station infrastructure.
PANEL 2 — Mira lays out HEAT / COMPRESSION / VIBRATION cards and starts the sequence while Zib watches her deliberately abuse the sample.
PANEL 3 — The fragment survives heat and compression; Mira keeps working without celebrating.
PANEL 4 — Sustained vibration chips the fragment.
PANEL 5 — Zib points at the damage and Mira confirms the obvious limitation: this is not a structural bracket.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: It holds under compression, but this sample falls apart when we warm it too far.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: That's a limitation I can work with. A miracle is harder to put in a work order.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: I never called it a miracle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: You called me in here to watch it happen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: That was because I thought you'd enjoy being right about one of the tests.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: I enjoyed it more when I didn't have to wear goggles.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: Zib builds a conventional temporary brace from approved clamp hardware and mesh. The residue fragment is used only as gap-filling material inside the brace. Middle image: Zib tightens the approved clamp. Closing image: The unit restarts. Status changes on the display.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib builds a conventional temporary brace from approved clamp hardware and mesh. The residue fragment is used only as gap-filling material inside the brace.
PANEL 2 — Astra watches closely.
PANEL 3 — Zib tightens the approved clamp.
PANEL 4 — Mira checks the configuration.
PANEL 5 — The unit restarts. Status changes on the display.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Approved brace, approved mesh, ordinary clamp. This isn't the material holding the weight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: It only fills the gap that kept opening. That's what the bench test suggested.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: If this works, I'm buying both of you a real meal. Somewhere that doesn't dispense it in spheres.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Check the pressure before you make reservations.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: It's steady.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: That was the most expensive sentence I've heard all day.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay, continuing the live temporary repair. Opening image: the repair enters monitored service. Middle image: Jax owns the interval work. Closing image: his small observation catches the first drift.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax watches the flow reader beside the restarted unit and logs the first monitored interval.
PANEL 2 — Astra checks the temporary tag while Jax shows her the handwritten ten-minute schedule he is already following.
PANEL 3 — At the next reading, Jax spots a two-millimeter shift before anyone else.
PANEL 4 — Zib isolates the unit immediately; Jax's hoped-for 'nothing' disappears into the next repair step.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: You want readings every interval? I can do that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I know you can. I'm asking whether you'll actually stay.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: You sound like Glorp. He still thinks I owe him a clean cup.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: He thinks you *owe* him one. There's a difference.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: Flow's drifting. Look at this.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Good. Don't touch anything; just keep watching it.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: Zib opens the brace again. Middle image: Jax holds the reader ready while Astra keeps the temporary authorization visible at the workbench. Closing image: Pixa's display shows measured flow and patch status only, without an explanatory headline.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib opens the brace again.
PANEL 2 — He adds more approved mesh and reduces the amount of residue filler.
PANEL 3 — Mira agrees.
PANEL 4 — Jax holds the reader ready while Astra keeps the temporary authorization visible at the workbench.
PANEL 5 — Zib restarts the unit.
PANEL 6 — Pixa's display shows measured flow and patch status only, without an explanatory headline.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Open it again. I don't like that drop.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: I thought we'd earned at least half an hour before the bad news.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: The material changed shape where we expected it to. Not enough to fail, but enough to matter.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Then change the support, not the story we tell ourselves.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: The second run has stabilized. I'm keeping both readings.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Good. No editing history to make the repair look prettier.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay, continuing the revised test. Opening image: the patch survives another cycle. Middle image: Mira and Zib agree on a narrow physical result. Closing image: Astra's caution and Brick's joke arrive at the same moment.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The revised brace completes another cycle while Mira and Zib inspect it together.
PANEL 2 — Zib names the modest result: the approved clamp held and the filler stayed out of the way.
PANEL 3 — Mira lets herself smile at the material result; Astra hears the phrase from across the bay and immediately limits the commercial framing.
PANEL 4 — Brick, already nearby, writes THE WEIRD THING GOT A JOB in his notebook.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Second cycle held. Narrowly, but it held.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: I'm comfortable leaving the conventional brace under monitoring.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Can we report that without telling central we invented a new industry?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: Industries have been founded on weaker evidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Brick, you're not making the brochure.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: A rejected commission. I'll survive.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: the physical findings are finally gathered in one place. Middle image: Astra prefers the small result until reporting becomes mandatory. Closing image: the real complication moves from repair to institutional visibility.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira builds a compact results board with heat, compression, vibration damage and installed configuration.
PANEL 2 — Astra visibly relaxes when Mira says the known result is small.
PANEL 3 — Mira turns the temporary-repair form toward Astra and points to the required material-event report.
PANEL 4 — Astra closes her eyes as the administrative consequence becomes unavoidable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: I thought you'd be happier. You kept asking me to find a use for the residue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I asked you to investigate it. I didn't ask corporate to put a price tag on your curiosity.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Do you know how long I've been doing good work nobody outside this station notices?

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Yes. I do. That's why I'm worried about what notice will cost.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: Glorp traces the temporary-deviation reporting path on a tablet. Middle image: Astra points at the report destination. Closing image: Zib shuts the wall panel.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp traces the temporary-deviation reporting path on a tablet.
PANEL 2 — Glorp looks up.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb meets Glorp's eyes over the tablet, antennae still and posture relaxed.
PANEL 4 — Astra points at the report destination.
PANEL 5 — Glorp shakes their head.
PANEL 6 — Zib shuts the wall panel.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: Once I mark this deviation, I can't guarantee it stays inside the maintenance file.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: Then say what actually happened. It's less frightening than people guessing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Zib, is the brace still sound?

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Yes. As long as nobody mistakes it for a permanent part.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: That's exactly the phrase I want in the report.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: And Mira's name. She did more than accidentally stand near it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Both names. The limits, too.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: the report creates the first direct Astra/Mira conflict. Middle image: both are protecting different risks around the same narrow finding. Closing image: the argument reveals they are closer than Astra feared.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra and Mira face each other across the workbench with the patched unit and report between them.
PANEL 2 — Mira argues for accurate reporting while Astra argues against turning one patch into a discovery story.
PANEL 3 — Mira makes clear that she was never proposing the larger claim; the disagreement narrows rather than escalating.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I know what the material did. What I don't know is what they'll expect next.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: You say that as though my discovery is a problem I caused.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: That's not what I meant.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Then say you're proud of me before you tell me to be careful.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I'm proud of you. I'm also afraid they're going to ask for another one.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay, continuing the Astra/Mira argument. Opening image: Mira asks for Astra's real fear. Middle image: Astra names the causal chain rather than speaking in abstractions. Closing image: both acknowledge the station's need without resolving the tension.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira asks Astra what she actually thinks will happen if the anomaly is reported.
PANEL 2 — Astra lays out the institutional chain: anomaly becomes category, category becomes target, target attracts budget.
PANEL 3 — Astra looks across the active maintenance bay as she explains that the budget will eventually dictate how to produce more.
PANEL 4 — Mira answers that the station needs money; Astra admits that is exactly what makes the temptation dangerous.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: When you came here, you told me this place could do interesting work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I thought it could. I still do. I also remember how quickly the headquarters people stopped listening.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: What did you think would happen?

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: That we'd get to tell them what mattered. Instead we learned to tell them what fit on one page.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Then let's write one page neither of us is embarrassed to sign.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay, continuing the same argument while work resumes. Opening image: Zib refuses to let the decision detach from the repair. Middle image: Astra and Mira literally share the work. Closing image: their reporting rule emerges while their hands are occupied.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib interrupts the argument from inside the actual repair and tells them to stop arguing like a meeting.
PANEL 2 — He hands Astra part of the brace and Mira the sensor lead, physically putting both back into the work.
PANEL 3 — Mira continues the reporting boundary while checking the sensor instead of facing Astra.
PANEL 4 — Astra holds the brace steady and adds that the report must include what the test does not support.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: You're both talking about who reads the report while I still have a wall open.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: The clamp needs another turn. I'm here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Give me the hold point.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: That's better. You can argue while your hands are doing something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: I'll write the actual test, including when it failed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: And I'll write the repair as temporary. Neither of us has to pretend.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: Glorp, Kreeb, Mira and Astra cluster around one terminal while the active maintenance bay remains visible behind them. Middle image: Kreeb nods. Closing image: Mira looks toward the patched unit.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Glorp, Kreeb, Mira and Astra cluster around one terminal while the active maintenance bay remains visible behind them.
PANEL 2 — The report shows the narrow temporary-use finding and its limits.
PANEL 3 — Glorp studies it.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb nods.
PANEL 5 — Astra rereads the screen.
PANEL 6 — Mira looks toward the patched unit.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: The system has a box for intended applications. We have one demonstrated application.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kreeb
dialogueInline.text: Put one, then. We can be pleased about one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: I am pleased. I was pleased yesterday, when the sample did something I didn't expect.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: And I am relieved we're not describing the crew as part of the manufacturing process.

dialogueInline.speaker: Glorp
dialogueInline.text: That's not the wording I was considering.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Good. Because they're terrible at manufacturing my patience.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: Jax arrives with the completed monitoring log. Middle image: Jax shrugs. Closing image: Astra signs.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax arrives with the completed monitoring log.
PANEL 2 — He hands it to Astra.
PANEL 3 — Astra checks the intervals.
PANEL 4 — Jax shrugs.
PANEL 5 — The terminal shows a blank STATION MANAGER SIGNATURE field above the SEND control.
PANEL 6 — Astra signs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: Here are the readings. I stayed for the extra cycle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Without being asked twice?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: Don't look so startled. Kreeb will tell you I'm delightful in the evenings.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: The drift stabilized after Zib changed the support.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Then this is the evidence we send.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: You'd think a quiet afternoon was a bigger discovery than the material.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Some days it is.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: the active crisis is over, leaving only routine monitoring. Middle image: Zib notices Jax staying voluntarily. Closing image: Jax's growth is shown through boring follow-through rather than a speech.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The maintenance bay is quiet during the next scheduled monitoring interval; Jax remains beside the reader after everyone else has moved on.
PANEL 2 — Zib passes through and tells him he can leave; Jax checks the clock instead.
PANEL 3 — Jax stays for the six-minute reading without making a ceremony of his own small change; the gauge remains inside the temporary band.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: You're still here? I thought your monitoring shift ended.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: It did. I wanted to see whether the next reading stayed level.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: You could have gone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jax Orien
dialogueInline.text: And miss the chance to tell you I was right? Don't be ridiculous.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: Astra and Mira perform the final read together. Middle image: Astra traces one sentence on the report with a fingertip, pausing over the highlighted causal wording. Closing image: Astra hits SEND herself.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra and Mira perform the final read together.
PANEL 2 — Astra points at a modifier.
PANEL 3 — Mira edits it.
PANEL 4 — Astra traces one sentence on the report with a fingertip, pausing over the highlighted causal wording.
PANEL 5 — Mira does not touch the screen.
PANEL 6 — Astra hits SEND herself.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: You crossed out 'unusual dust.' Thank you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I was being cautious. It sounded like something you'd find under a vending machine.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: You have found me under a vending machine. That's not a scientific category.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Narrow result. Repeatable under these conditions. Failures included.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: And my name under yours.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: It was your discovery. You can watch me press send if you want.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: I absolutely do.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay, continuing directly from the final report send. Opening image: the crew gets the acknowledgement they wanted. Middle image: the forwarding line changes its meaning. Closing image: the issue's next engine arrives as a bureaucratic consequence.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The observational-report acknowledgement arrives almost immediately.
PANEL 2 — Astra exhales at RECEIVED before a second line appears beneath it.
PANEL 3 — FORWARDED TO: RESOURCE EFFICIENCY REVIEW changes Astra's face before anyone comments.
PANEL 4 — Mira registers the speed of escalation while Brick closes his notebook and names the institutional appetite.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: They acknowledged it. That's a relief.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: They've forwarded it to commercial review.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I was relieved for almost four seconds.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brick Talos
dialogueInline.text: A remarkably short honeymoon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Don't look at me. I asked for recognition, not a product launch.

summary: Primary composition: 6-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: One inspection cycle later, the repaired unit hums. The temporary tag is still prominent. Middle image: Zib closes the panel. Closing image: Pixa's screen lights. Nobody speaks.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — One inspection cycle later, the repaired unit hums. The temporary tag is still prominent.
PANEL 2 — Zib checks procurement.
PANEL 3 — Astra points at the patch.
PANEL 4 — Zib closes the panel.
PANEL 5 — Mira seals another physical sample.
PANEL 6 — Pixa's screen lights. Nobody speaks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Zib “Sgotcha” Diaz
dialogueInline.text: Brace is still holding. The replacement remains nineteen days away, apparently forever.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: I've already asked for an updated delivery date.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: I want another sample, but not while the thing is running.

dialogueInline.speaker: Pixa
dialogueInline.text: Acknowledgement received from central materials review.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: Leave it in the queue. I want one ordinary hour.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: You know that's the sentence that makes the next message arrive.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Maintenance Bay. Opening image: commercial interest becomes explicit. Middle image: Mira and Astra do not reopen the reporting decision. Closing image: Astra's fear is confirmed without making the earlier choice wrong.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra expands the preliminary-interest notice at her terminal after the next inspection cycle.
PANEL 2 — COMMERCIAL INTEREST and the station-value language sit together while Astra absorbs the exact framing.
PANEL 3 — Mira stays beside her and restates that accurate reporting was still necessary.
PANEL 4 — Astra looks through the glass toward the functioning maintenance bay and admits she only wanted one more day before the anomaly acquired a department.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: They want a commercial feasibility call.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: On a sample we've used once, inside an ordinary brace?

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Yes. I know. But I'd still like to be on the call.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: You should be. It was your work.

dialogueInline.speaker: Mira Klare
dialogueInline.text: Good. I also want you there when they misunderstand it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Astra Vega
dialogueInline.text: That part I can guarantee.
